statement: A set of points is convex if it contains every line segment between two points in the set. Equivalently, a real-valued function is convex if the line segment between any two distinct points on the graph of the function lies above or on the graph of the function between the two points, which is equivalent to its epigraph (the set of points on or above the graph of the function) being a convex set.

symbols.meaning: distinct points in the set or domain of the function
line segment connecting points x and y
Hessian matrix of second partial derivatives of f

properties.property: A real-valued function is convex if and only if its epigraph (the set of points on or above the graph of the function) is a convex set.
properties.why: epigraph characterization equates functional convexity with geometric set convexity

properties.property: For a twice continuously differentiable function f, if the Hessian ∇²f(x) is positive semidefinite (or f''(x) ≥ 0 on the real line), then f is convex.
properties.why: second derivative lower bound with m = 0 implies convexity

properties.property: The intersection of any collection of convex sets is itself convex.
properties.why: convex subsets of a vector space form a complete lattice under intersection and convex hull joins

properties.property: If C is a convex set in a topological vector space, its closure Cl C and its interior Int C are both convex.
properties.why: topological closure and interior operations preserve convexity

properties.property: The convex hull of the Minkowski sum of sets equals the Minkowski sum of their convex hulls: Conv(S₁ + S₂) = Conv(S₁) + Conv(S₂).
properties.why: Minkowski summation and forming convex hulls are commuting operations

properties.property: The Minkowski sum of two compact convex sets is compact, and the sum of a compact convex set and a closed convex set is closed.
properties.why: compactness and closedness are preserved under Minkowski addition of convex sets

assumptions.assumption: The ambient space is a geometric space or vector space equipped with linear segments {tx + (1-t)y : t ∈ [0, 1]}.
assumptions.breaks_when: The space lacks linear or affine structure, preventing the definition of straight line segments between points.

assumptions.assumption: For Hessian-based convexity characterizations, the function must be twice continuously differentiable on its domain.
assumptions.breaks_when: The function lacks first or second derivatives at points in its domain (such as f(x) = |x| at x = 0).

failure_modes.mode: Domain discontinuity or singularity interrupting global convexity
failure_modes.signature: A function is convex on separate intervals but fails to be convex on their union.
failure_modes.cause: A singularity (such as at x = 0 for f(x) = 1/x²) creates a discontinuity preventing line segments from remaining above the graph across the entire domain.

failure_modes.mode: Geometric non-convexity via indents or hollow regions
failure_modes.signature: There exist two points in the set such that the line segment connecting them passes outside the set.
failure_modes.cause: The set has an indent, hollow, or non-convex boundary geometry (such as a crescent shape).
